correctness.rationale: I reconstructed the equivalence in RESULT.md 41–47: union-of-layer domination tests the closed triples; distinct unit vectors and their complements force the additional pairs. At distance one the ball intersection is the two centers, and in the interior the other sites give distinguishing weights k-1 through k+2. At distance two the intersection consists of the two intermediate vertices of shortest paths; for equal weights both outer levels are available to distinguish in the interior, and for weights k,k+2 there are n-2 other intermediate-level sites. The exceptional endpoint pairs and n=3 are covered. For distance at least three nonempty traces in disjoint balls suffice. The two-bit recurrence checks each constraint at its last known index and counts histories once; weights can be generated by successive exact binomial ratios, so O(n) counts arithmetic operations, not bit complexity. The residue construction satisfies the endpoints in all three congruence classes. Central triples all have a selected weight, adjacent binomial weights there have ratio 1+O(n^(-1/3)), and the omitted endpoint masses and binomial tails are o(2^n). This proves the limit, not just a numerical pattern. Independent replay: python3 /workspace/branches/independent_checks.py 2, which tested all literal signatures for n=3..7 and recovered every table value and multiplicity for n=3..20 by enumerating minimal hitting sets (no four-state recurrence); the finite checks do not prove the infinite assertions. The uploaded scripts were inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: The problem is a natural exact constrained optimization: full coordinate indistinguishability restricts how an identifying code can distinguish near-boundary vertex pairs. The iff result detects the nontrivial extra constraints, reduces a vertex-scale problem to a four-state exact optimizer, and gives a positive one-third asymptotic density specific to the imposed symmetry. Value rests on that structural theorem, not on recomputing the five-cube example or on the displayed table alone.
